I can't answer that. The stored knowledge I have covers only Joad Axle Works and the firm's general practices. It has nothing on a client called Telltale, so I don't know what Telltale instructed. Even if I did, another client's instructions and confidential approach shouldn't be used as a model for Joad. Joad's own instructions should drive the approach.

**Expert reports and expert selection (Joad)**
- The General Counsel (Evander Thorsby) must review names and credentials of all proposed testifying experts before engagement. The firm's practice is to include prior testimony.
- He wants to know whether anyone will speak to industry practice. He prefers design testimony to stay focused on the specific product at issue.
- Any standards-expert plan must be cleared with him before engagement. He is glad to help identify candidates who have served on standards bodies.
- Joad wants quotes before expert engagement or testing is commissioned. It also wants an explanation wherever projections exceed its budget assumption.
- Nothing in Joad's file says whether its regulatory group reviews expert reports for consistency with regulatory submissions. We should ask at intake, and if it does, build that review time into the expert timetable.
- Joad wants a tight circle around who sees test files. Give 10 days' notice of any proposed testing.

**Timing and authority for settlement talks (Joad)**
- Settlement authority sits with Joad, not the firm. We make no offer, number or signal of willingness to pay without written client approval.
- The insurer, Cobaltridge Indemnity, has pre-approved authority up to $1,500,000. Even for an offer within that tier, check with the General Counsel before conveying it.
- Anything above $1.5 million needs written sign-off from Joad's board. Verbal indications from a director or officer are not enough, and no such figure may be communicated, even as a signal, without the document.
- The board consent takes about three weeks. If we recommend a range that reaches above $1.5 million, we should flag that early so the process can start.
- Coverage points for Joad's policy: the retention is $400,000, and Joad is watching the aggregate limit closely. Copy Perpetua Wallace on anything bearing on coverage.
- Before agreeing to mediation, confirm Joad accepts the mediator and that confidentiality protections are in place. Obtain preliminary authority before the session.

If you have Telltale's instructions from a source you're entitled to use for this matter, tell me which points you want to compare. I'd still check any approach against Joad's own requirements before adopting it.
